result.title: Refining and Aligning Clinical Reasoning with Health Guidelines via Formal Constraints
result.summary: Clinical reasoning from incomplete or conflicting patient evidence must account for low-probability but high-risk concerns while remaining grounded in health guidelines. We introduce VerClin, an explainable framework that extracts guideline conditions, exclusions, recommendations, and priorities into executable knowledge and represents patient conversations as scoped cases. A deterministic four-valued reasoner produces traceable guideline matches while preserving uncertainty and enforcing exclusions. Multiple specialty agents then screen matched guidelines for case applicability, and a consultation model synthesizes accepted guidance through specialty recommendations and a sentence-preserving formal-constraint channel. We present accepted guidance in ascending order of the sum of its priority and trigger-strength ranks, which can surface high-risk guidance with weaker triggers. VerClin outperforms direct generation and Top-5 RAG on HealthBench Hard and HealthBench Professional. On the LLMEval-Med subset, it outperforms direct generation and ties Top-5 RAG. Component analyses further examine semantic closure, example-guided refinement, specialty screening, and constraint-conditioned delivery.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 VerClin：将临床指南的条件、排除项、推荐与优先级抽取为可执行知识，用四值确定性推理器给出可追溯的指南匹配并保留不确定性，再由多专科 agent 筛选适用性、经形式约束通道生成建议；在 HealthBench Hard/Professional 上优于直接生成与 Top-5 RAG。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「保留不确定性并强制排除」的显式推理状态、专科证据适用性筛选与排序呈现，可能为 LVR 中的视觉证据筛选、状态不确定性表示及可追溯的停止与弃权决策提供远域参照；但论文为纯文本临床场景、无视觉或多模态成分，可供核查迁移价值。
